objective.text: Make scheduled work resumable and idempotent instead of assuming onOneServer guarantees completion.

difficulty.rationale: Separate occurrence election from recovery of a partially completed business operation.

runtime.sapi: Isolated CLI Laravel harness unless another context is explicitly stated
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; UTC; no external services or application data

stem: A nightly import uses onOneServer but crashes after committing 4,000 of 10,000 per-item results. It must resume without duplicating completed results. Which design adds the missing recovery boundary?

options.text: Persist stable per-item results and resume from durable progress.
options.rationale: Single-server election does not persist completion. Durable item identity and progress allow a later attempt to continue safely after partial success.

options.text: Keep the last processed item only in a static PHP property on the scheduler process.
options.rationale: Process-local progress disappears with the crash and cannot identify what a replacement process has already completed.
options.misconception: Process-local progress disappears with the crash and cannot identify what a replacement process has already completed.

options.text: Increase the mutex expiration until it covers the whole night, with no stored progress.
options.rationale: A longer lock cannot reconstruct completed work after a crash and can delay recovery.
options.misconception: A longer lock cannot reconstruct completed work after a crash and can delay recovery.

options.text: Rely on onOneServer to remember the last processed item and resume the PHP loop.
options.rationale: The scheduler lock does not capture application loop state or a business checkpoint.
options.misconception: The scheduler lock does not capture application loop state or a business checkpoint.
